- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid underestimating the dip — add 2–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizons, if recent 5-day average is rising, model tends to overestimate — apply downward bias of 1–3% on forecast tail.
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term volatility (e.g., alternating +0.53/-0.23), model overfits noise — smooth forecast by 1–2% downward.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in 3 consecutive days, adjust next forecast down by 2–4% to reflect momentum correction.
- If sentiment is flat (0.0–0.2) and forecast is trending, reduce forecast slope — assume low conviction leads to slower price movement.
- For high sentiment + high recent price, forecast often peaks too early — delay peak by 1–3 days and reduce magnitude by 3–5%.
